source: Screenshots matched by visible slide content to the supplied lesson transcript; source PNG names are listed for newly added assets. Unmatched screenshots are not displayed.

mapped_screenshots.title: Core Basics and the Restaurant Analogy
mapped_screenshots.alt: Dark slide reading Give an AI a goal, a messy folder, a browser, and 30 minutes.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The slide’s opening challenge: define a goal and give the system the context and time to work.

mapped_screenshots.title: Core Basics and the Restaurant Analogy
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide contrasts answers, assists, acts, and finishes as stages of AI capability.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The session’s progression from getting answers to completing work.

mapped_screenshots.title: The Restaurant Workflow & Delegation
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide listing four moves: understand, delegate, watch, and operationalize.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The four moves the trainer uses to explain delegation.

mapped_screenshots.title: The Restaurant Workflow & Delegation
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide about Astra continuing work while one question waits, with research, prepare, and build steps.
mapped_screenshots.caption: Related session slide about work continuing while a question waits. The transcript does not specify its prioritization rules.

mapped_screenshots.title: Answers vs. Completed Work
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide states GPT-6 Astra is a reasoning model built for end-to-end work and the useful unit is the verified outcome.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The slide makes the session’s answer-versus-outcome distinction explicit.

mapped_screenshots.title: Answers vs. Completed Work
mapped_screenshots.alt: Comparison slide: chat asks for content while delegation asks for completion.
mapped_screenshots.caption: A concise visual distinction between asking for content and delegating a finished result.

mapped_screenshots.title: AGI, Model, Harness, and Workflow
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide titled Astra is evidence of progress, not proof of AGI, comparing model, harness, and workflow.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The session’s three-part framework: model, harness, and workflow.

mapped_screenshots.title: Live Demonstration & ChatGPT Work Interface
mapped_screenshots.alt: Screenshot of the GPT Work interface showing a model and effort selection menu.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The model and effort controls shown during the live interface demonstration.

mapped_screenshots.title: Live Demonstration & ChatGPT Work Interface
mapped_screenshots.alt: Screenshot of the detailed prompt requesting a comparison of six AI operations programs with verified fields and exact links.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The research request and its comparison criteria as entered for the demonstration.

mapped_screenshots.title: The Execution Loop
mapped_screenshots.alt: Diagram of answer, reason, act, and verify steps.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The session’s execution loop, arranged as four visible stages.

mapped_screenshots.title: The Execution Loop
mapped_screenshots.alt: Circular process diagram for delegated missions, showing understand, report, plan, verify, inspect, and act.
mapped_screenshots.caption: A companion slide expands the delegated task into a repeating mission loop.

mapped_screenshots.title: Architecture Layers of Astra
mapped_screenshots.alt: Layer diagram showing model, context, tools, permissions, feedback, and evaluation.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The layer diagram associated with the architecture discussion.

mapped_screenshots.title: Task Results and Baseline Use Cases
mapped_screenshots.alt: Screenshot of the generated AI operations program comparison table.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The result table shown after the research prompt. The transcript’s stated total and named providers do not fully agree.

mapped_screenshots.title: Native Capabilities and Deployment Environments
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide titled What goes in, what comes out, showing text and images in and text out, with audio and video note.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The session slide about input and output types. Its statements are presented here as the trainer’s explanation.

mapped_screenshots.title: Native Capabilities and Deployment Environments
mapped_screenshots.alt: Comparison of ChatGPT conversation, Codex local files and tools, and API custom product environments.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The three environments named in the transcript.

mapped_screenshots.title: Choosing Effort Levels
mapped_screenshots.alt: Chart comparing low, medium, high, extra high, and max reasoning effort levels.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The effort-level guide shown in the session.

mapped_screenshots.title: Managing Context & Prompt Quality
mapped_screenshots.alt: Screenshot of a staged task response with evidence, rejected positions, approval, and a budget scenario.
mapped_screenshots.caption: A structured task exchange illustrating staged instructions and checkpoints.

mapped_screenshots.title: Automated Email Processing & The Tool Multiplier
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide grouping tools into search, create, compute, operate, connect, and route.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The tool categories used in the session to explain the multiplier effect.

mapped_screenshots.title: Automated Email Processing & The Tool Multiplier
mapped_screenshots.alt: Screenshot of an email-processing task prompt asking for a supplier email summary and recommended action.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The supplier-email example shown in the interface; the transcript describes summarizing, checking, and drafting or logging.

mapped_screenshots.title: Automated Email Processing & The Tool Multiplier
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide comparing direct tools, computer use, and human handoff as ways to act.
mapped_screenshots.caption: Related slide with additional tool-choice guidance that the transcript excerpt does not expand.

mapped_screenshots.title: Benchmarks and Limitations
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide lists ambiguity, missing truth, prompt injection, accountability, and variability as remaining limits.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The slide includes additional limitations—missing truth, prompt injection, accountability, and variability—that are not explained in the transcript text. They are identified here as slide content, not transcript-derived claims.

mapped_screenshots.title: Structuring Prompts for Autonomous Execution
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide comparing a weak request with a strong, evidence-based bounded delegation brief.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The contrast supports the lesson’s focus on outcome, evidence, boundaries, and a clear stop before publishing or spending.

mapped_screenshots.title: Structuring Prompts for Autonomous Execution
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide explaining that a real use case tests research, analysis, judgment, creation, and verification.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The source’s launch-planning example spans multiple capabilities and ends with verification.

mapped_screenshots.title: Execution, Permissions, and Safety Guardrails
mapped_screenshots.alt: Permission-design slide assigning read and draft actions to automatic execution, edits to checkpoints, and external communication or spending to human-only authority.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The screenshot makes the source’s three permission tiers concrete with examples of read, draft, edit, communicate, and spend actions.

mapped_screenshots.title: Execution, Permissions, and Safety Guardrails
mapped_screenshots.alt: Human-in-the-loop slide placing checkpoints at plan, evidence, decision, and action boundaries.
mapped_screenshots.caption: Review decisions that change consequences instead of reviewing every routine step.

mapped_screenshots.title: Execution, Permissions, and Safety Guardrails
mapped_screenshots.alt: Acceptance-criteria slide defining correct, complete, coherent, usable, and safe work.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The source’s completion criteria expressed as checks that can be evaluated.

mapped_screenshots.title: Session Intelligence for Better Workshops
mapped_screenshots.alt: Title slide introducing Mission 02: Session Intelligence.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The session-intelligence mission title, matched to the source section.

mapped_screenshots.title: Session Intelligence for Better Workshops
mapped_screenshots.alt: Timeline aligning attendance, reactions, chat, polls, and transcript streams.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The visual shows the multiple session data streams the source says to analyze together.

mapped_screenshots.title: Stress-Testing Recommendations with Self-Critique
mapped_screenshots.alt: Slide titled Make Astra argue against itself, challenging a pitch and asking for alternative explanations and discriminating evidence.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The slide illustrates challenging a recommendation before treating correlation as a decision.

mapped_screenshots.title: Stress-Testing Recommendations with Self-Critique
mapped_screenshots.alt: Prompt asking for a project-management tool recommendation with context, constraints, authority, evidence, and a definition of done.
mapped_screenshots.caption: An example structured recommendation request that can be followed by the source’s self-critique step.

mapped_screenshots.title: When to Use a High-Cost Model
mapped_screenshots.alt: Diagram contrasting low-coordination tasks with more coordinated end-to-end missions.
mapped_screenshots.caption: The visual mirrors the source’s rule of thumb for reserving higher-cost models.
